subtype: Approach: pads every task so heavily that work expands to fill it [Pitfall]
passage:
Subject: what I found on the Q2 estimates

Hi Payal,

You asked why the Q2 launch was late again, so I went through the tracker. When I made the estimates, I put a big cushion on every task, so each one had ten days for what is really four days of work. The team relaxed. Nobody started early, and most tasks were touched for the first time in the last two days before their dates. Testing came at the very end and squeezed everything. The days I padded never turned into spare days. I believed the padding would keep everyone calm, but calm turned into slow.

Can we talk on Monday about what a better estimate could look like?

Gurpreet

qa.q: How many days did each task get for what was really four days of work?
qa.a: Each task had ten days for what is really four days of work.

qa.q: What did Gurpreet expect the padding to do?
qa.a: Gurpreet expected the padding to keep everyone calm, but the calm turned into slowness.

qa.q: What could Gurpreet do instead of padding every task?
qa.a: Gurpreet could keep honest estimates for each task and hold one shared cushion near the end for real delays, so tasks do not stretch to fill their days.

qa.q: How might Payal feel on reading this email?
qa.a: Payal, who asked why the launch was late again, may feel relieved to get a clear answer, and perhaps frustrated that the launch slipped.

grounding: Shows a heavy cushion added to every estimate, so the team relaxes and still finishes at the last minute.
